## Summary

After the `ws-*` skill renames (e.g. `ws-write-spec` ΓåÆ `ws-spec-write`, `ws-sync-spec` ΓåÆ `ws-spec-update`, `ws-multi-spec` ΓåÆ `ws-spec-multi`, `ws-local-spec-provider` ΓåÆ `ws-spec-provider-local`, `ws-verify-plan` ΓåÆ `ws-plan-verify`, `ws-github-provider` ΓåÆ `ws-spec-provider-github`, `ws-azure-devops-provider` ΓåÆ `ws-spec-provider-azure-devops`, `ws-write-plan` ΓåÆ `ws-plan-write`, `ws-update-plan-implementation` ΓåÆ `ws-plan-update`, `ws-interview` ΓåÆ `ws-plan-interview`), a consumer tree installed **before** the renames keeps stale references in managed files. Running the installer `update` refreshes skill bodies but does not migrate these references, so a `ws-check-harness` audit keeps flagging retired ids. A related gap: a global (`--global`) hybrid install leaves no local `ws-shared/AGENTS.md`, while `config.json` `rules.harness` defaults to that local path.

Found via `ws-check-harness` Phases 0ΓÇô5c (Install mode: consumer, hybrid global+local). All four mechanical gates exit 0 (`check_duplicates`, `measure_harness`, `check_shell_quoting`, `check_pipeline_handoff`); `configure_autoload.py --check` reports ok.

## 1. Managed `ws-shared/autoload.md` still cites retired skill ids

The project-local `ws-shared/autoload.md` (shipped template copy) references retired ids throughout ΓÇö Specs vocabulary table (`ws-local-spec-provider`, `ws-write-spec`, `ws-sync-spec`, `ws-multi-spec`), Specs skill router links (`../ws-write-spec/SKILL.md`, `../ws-local-spec-provider/SKILL.md`, `../ws-sync-spec/SKILL.md`, `../ws-multi-spec/SKILL.md`), keyword map, Hub contracts (`../ws-verify-plan/SKILL.md`, `ws-verify-plan`), flow diagram (`ws-github-provider` / `ws-azure-devops-provider` fetch), and complement rules ΓÇö while the canonical global hub uses the new `ws-spec-*` / `ws-plan-verify` ids.

The `../ws-<retired-id>/SKILL.md` Markdown targets are phantom: they exist neither under the project `{skillsRoot}` nor under the global skills root, so they fail Phase 2 existence checks even with hybrid resolution. Local projects must not hand-edit this managed template, so there is no clean consumer-side fix.

**Expected:** installer `update` refreshes managed hub templates (`autoload.md`, and any other template embedding skill ids/links) to the canonical ids, or ships an id-migration step for them alongside skill-folder renames.

## 2. `installed-skills.json` retains retired ids

The installer-written tracking file still lists `ws-interview`, `ws-verify-plan`, `ws-write-plan`, `ws-update-plan-implementation`, `ws-sync-spec`, `ws-multi-spec`, `ws-local-spec-provider`, `ws-github-provider`, `ws-azure-devops-provider`, plus legacy bare ids (`azure-devops`, `caveman`, `code-review`, `fix-pr`, `plan-us`, `us-delivery-workflow`).

**Expected:** `update` prunes retired ids (or maps them to canonical ids) in `installed-skills.json` so future updates/uninstalls operate on real skills.

## 3. Global-hybrid install: `rules.harness` target missing locally

`config.json` `rules.harness` defaults to `.agents/skills/ws-shared/AGENTS.md`, but a global install leaves the project-local `ws-shared/` with only consumer data files (`config.json`, `autoload.md`, `STACK.md`, `MEMORY.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`) ΓÇö no `AGENTS.md` (the global hub has it). Agents reading the configured local path fail and must fall back to the global hub manually.

**Expected:** either the installer seeds a thin local hub pointer for global-hybrid layouts, or the `rules.harness` default/comment documents the `{globalSkillsRoot}` fallback.

## Repro (generic)

1. Consumer tree installed before the renames, skills installed globally (`--global`), project-local `ws-shared/` holding consumer data only.
2. Run `ws-check-harness` (or `rg` for `ws-write-spec|ws-sync-spec|ws-multi-spec|ws-local-spec-provider|ws-verify-plan|ws-github-provider|ws-azure-devops-provider|ws-interview|ws-write-plan|ws-update-plan-implementation` across `ws-shared/autoload.md`, `ws-shared/installed-skills.json`, `ws-shared/config.json`).
3. Observe retired-id hits in managed files + missing local `ws-shared/AGENTS.md` vs `rules.harness`.
title: Update leaves retired skill ids in ws-shared/autoload.md + installed-skills.json; global-hybrid install has no local ws-shared/AGENTS.md for rules.harness
